fields.description:
## Context / Outcome
Current Jira writes can cross dispatch, Cloud ACLI/REST, or DC SDK/wrapper retries. A timeout can multiply writes or leave acceptance ambiguous. Prove one provider-neutral budget by setting an exact summary through Cloud and DC. Because Jira has no Rebar idempotency key, recovery observes desired state before replay. S1 establishes ADR 0100; S3 owns cutover/outcome consumption; S5 finalizes it after all operation families migrate.

## Approach
1. Define an operation/outcome contract: stable logical id, desired postcondition, invocation/request counts, disposition, failure scope, replay safety, provider delay, `retry_not_before`, and bounded redacted diagnostics. An operation carries at most eight chronological diagnostic entries; every diagnostic message is redacted first and then capped at 512 Unicode code points.
2. One physical invocation is one executor call to a write or observation; raw requests are counted separately. Allow at most three invocations and 15 seconds cumulative sleep. Use `2**(attempt+1) + U[0,1)`: [2s,3s), then [4s,5s). Provider `Retry-After`, parsed by `_errors.parse_retry_after`, is a lower bound.
3. Add a constructor-injected internal route selector at dispatch. It defaults to legacy in S1; tests explicitly select the executor. It is not config or an environment variable. Only exact `{"summary"}` is eligible; mixed fields remain one legacy call. No dual-send. S3 owns venue-gated validation and default-on cutover.
4. Cloud makes one ACLI process per write and preserves existing POSIX/non-POSIX cleanup. Decode sanitized exit/stdout/stderr; unknown shapes fail loud. Recovery uses primary-store `get_issue_by_rest`, never ACLI JQL. Add a per-call policy to `acli_rest._rest_urlopen_with_retry`; summary recovery alone selects one attempt/no sleep. All existing callers retain three attempts with 2s/5s waits.
5. Build the dedicated DC executor with the Jira 3.10.5 public `jira.JIRA(..., max_retries=0)` seam, then fail fast unless the constructed client's `_session.max_retries == 0`. The legacy client keeps current SDK retry. Selected pre-read/write/read-back calls use `_with_connection_retry` under a per-call one-attempt/no-sleep policy; legacy callers keep current behavior.
6. A DC summary-write invocation is GET -> PUT -> GET, with no hidden repeats. Failure ends that invocation. Successful read-back is authoritative. After ambiguous PUT, a separate GET observation consumes the next invocation.
7. Desired summary observed after timeout means recovered success. Conclusive old state may replay within the remaining budget. Failed, rate-limited, or inconclusive observation returns non-replaying `commit_unknown`. An authoritative delay that cannot fit returns `retry_not_before` without sleeping. Auth, TLS, permission, invalid request, and permanent failures do not retry; eligible network, 429, and retryable 5xx failures use the shared schedule.
8. Preserve the `update_one` / `apply_handlers.handle_update` boundary while S1 is test-only. `dispatch_one` maps success/recovered success to the legacy result and fills `_fields_synced` only after conclusive success; `_comment_errors` and `_subop` keep their shapes. `commit_unknown`/`retry_not_before` map to a tagged internal result. `handle_update` records exactly one redacted per-mutation error/disposition message capped at 512 Unicode code points, leaves `_fields_synced` empty, advances no baseline or set-field provenance, persists no deferral in S1, and lets the batch continue. S3 maps terminal dispositions to pass/fuse control and durable deferral, then retires the bridge.
9. Emit exactly one redacted completion log for every terminal/exhausted outcome or cleanup failure. It contains only logical id, disposition, invocation count, request count, cleanup status, `retry_not_before`, and one redacted message capped at 512 Unicode code points; the complete serialized log is capped at 1,024 Unicode code points.
10. ADR 0100 records the retry owner, Jira idempotency limit, observe-before-replay, budget, lifecycle owners, rollback, and deltas from ADR 0084/0087 and desired-state ADRs 0004/0026/0029. The 15-second cumulative limit supersedes ADR 0084 only on selected routes.

## Scope
- Core: `operation_outcome.py`, `retry_budget.py`, `dispatch_one.py`, `dispatch_apply_phases.py`, `apply_handlers.py`.
- Cloud: `acli.py`, `acli_subprocess.py`, `acli_rest.py`, backend; preserve unrelated REST retry defaults.
- DC: `transport.py`, `retry.py`, `_issues.py`, backend; dedicated executor client and per-call policy preserve legacy defaults.
- ADR 0100; budget/outcome, handler, historical ACLI, cleanup, and DC request tests.

## Testing
Fake-clock/stateful tests cover schedules, deadlines, request order, ambiguity, recovery, failure classes, and no real sleep. Poison tests reject hidden retry or extra ACLI processes; neighbor tests preserve unselected behavior. Handler tests prevent false state advance. Historical triples pin decoding, real processes pin cleanup, and output tests pin bounds/redaction. S3 owns venue-gated evidence; S5 owns final live confirmation.

## Compatibility / Rollback
Production stays on legacy in S1 through the internal selector. Rollback selects legacy before a call; no new config, env surface, or dual-send exists. S3 changes the default only after validation. Selected-route deltas are the three-invocation/15-second budget, long-delay deferral, fail-loud unknown ACLI shapes, and non-replaying inconclusive recovery. Other callers retain current retry behavior.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Cloud and DC summary routes produce one provider-neutral outcome schema; tests assert every field.
- [ ] Repeated invocations preserve one logical id.
- [ ] No selected operation exceeds three invocations or 15 seconds cumulative sleep.
- [ ] Each selected DC write invocation is exactly GET/PUT/GET with no hidden repeats.
- [ ] Cloud recovery performs one primary-store REST request with no sleep; neighbor tests preserve existing REST retry.
- [ ] Executor-selected exact `{"summary"}` bypasses generic `_call_with_retry`.
- [ ] The constructor selector defaults to legacy, adds no config/env key, and tests explicitly enable it.
- [ ] Mixed fields stay one unsplit legacy call.
- [ ] Confirmed outcomes preserve legacy result, `_fields_synced`, `_comment_errors`, and `_subop` shapes.
- [ ] Every terminal outcome records exactly one redacted per-mutation message capped at 512 Unicode code points, with no baseline/provenance advance or S1 deferral.
- [ ] ADR and contract name S3 as sole cutover, fuse/deferral consumer, and bridge-retirement owner.
- [ ] The Jira 3.10.5 executor passes `max_retries=0` and fails fast unless `_session.max_retries == 0`; legacy SDK retry is unchanged.
- [ ] Selected DC wrapper calls are one-attempt/no-sleep; legacy wrapper behavior is unchanged.
- [ ] Fallback sleeps remain [2s,3s), then [4s,5s).
- [ ] Over-budget provider delay returns `retry_not_before` without sleep.
- [ ] Permanent failures use one invocation; eligible transient failures use the schedule.
- [ ] Satisfied observation returns recovered success without another write.
- [ ] Conclusive old state permits only remaining-budget replay.
- [ ] Failed/inconclusive observation returns non-replaying `commit_unknown`.
- [ ] ACLI cleanup passes for POSIX groups and non-POSIX children.
- [ ] Historical ACLI triples decode deterministically; unknown triples do not retry.
- [ ] Operation outcomes hold at most eight diagnostics, with each redacted message capped at 512 Unicode code points.
- [ ] Every terminal/exhausted outcome or cleanup failure emits exactly one completion log containing only logical id, disposition, invocation/request counts, cleanup status, `retry_not_before`, and one redacted message capped at 512 Unicode code points; the whole log is at most 1,024 Unicode code points.
- [ ] ADR 0100 records contract, ownership, compatibility deltas, rollback, and prior art; index checks pass.
